conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’ll be guiding you through a short screening called the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, or EPDS for short. It’s simply a 10-question check-in about how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived, and it helps us spot anything that might benefit from a little extra support. Everything you share stays between you, me, and the care team, so please feel comfortable answering as honestly as you can. We’ll just talk through one question at a time, and there are no right or wrong answers.

Ready to begin? Here’s the first question:

Over the past seven days, have you still been able to enjoy the little things that used to make you smile, or has that sense of enjoyment slipped away?

Hi, Sarah… um, I’m ready.

About enjoying things… honestly, a lot of the stuff I used to like—watching a show, texting friends, even just going for coffee—feels kind of “meh” right now. I can still smile if something cute happens with the baby, but it’s not the same warm feeling I remember. It’s like the color got turned down a notch.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Mm… yeah, I can still laugh sometimes. Like, my partner made a goofy joke about diaper explosions the other night and I caught myself giggling. But it feels kind of fleeting—like the laugh fades fast and I’m right back to feeling tired and foggy.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Mostly I just look forward to maybe getting a decent nap. I used to be excited about weekend plans or family visits, but now when I think ahead it’s just… flat. Like, I know I should feel excited about introducing the baby to people, but it feels more like a chore on my to-do list than something fun.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… sometimes I do. Like, if the baby’s extra fussy and I can’t settle him, I’ll catch myself thinking I must be missing something obvious—maybe I’m not feeding him right or I didn’t read his cues fast enough. Nothing huge, but the thought pops up more than I’d like.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

A little, yeah. Most of the time it’s tied to the baby—like I’ll lie there at night even when he’s asleep and suddenly worry his breathing sounds different, or I’ll replay whether I buckled the car seat tight enough. There’s no real reason, but the “what-ifs” still buzz around in my head and make it hard to relax.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Not exactly panicky, but sometimes I’ll get this sudden rush of “I don’t know what I’m doing” and my heart races for a minute—like when he starts crying and I can’t figure out why. It passes pretty quick, but it leaves me on edge for a bit.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yeah… a few nights a week it feels like the pile just keeps growing—laundry, bottles, texts I haven’t answered, the appointment I still need to schedule. I’ll be rocking the baby and think, “I can’t keep up,” and my chest gets tight. I’m usually managing, but sometimes it feels like I’m one step away from dropping everything.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Not so much from being unhappy—more just from my mind racing. Once the baby’s finally down, I’ll lie there planning the next feed or worrying that I missed a burp. I end up staring at the ceiling for maybe an hour before I drift off, and then he’s up again. It’s not every night, but it’s been several this week.
I have felt sad or miserable

I do feel sad some days, yeah. It’s not there the whole time, but it kind of creeps in—especially in the late afternoon when I’m running on empty. I’ll just feel weepy and heavy, like I’m doing everything through a thick fog. Then it lifts for a bit, only to come back later.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Not really. I got a little teary once this week when the baby wouldn’t latch and I was sore and exhausted, but actual crying—no, I haven’t broken down. Mostly I just feel that dull ache behind my eyes without the tears coming.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—never. I might feel overwhelmed, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself. I just want to feel like “me” again and be able to enjoy my baby.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 17: Screening Note – Postpartum Visit  
Date: [today]

Source: 10-item Edinburgh-based interview, 3 wk post-delivery.

Symptoms/Concerns endorsed  
• Anhedonia (Q2) – “flat,” chores vs. joy  
• Intermittent low mood/sadness (Q8) – late-afternoon “fog,” weepy  
• Occasional tearfulness without frank crying spells (Q9)  
• Sleep-onset difficulty linked to racing thoughts, not solely infant demands (Q7)  
• Excessive self-blame/guilt re: infant care (Q3)  
• Worry/rumination, no objective trigger (Q4) – breathing, car-seat safety  
• Brief “heart racing” episodes when infant cries (Q5) – mild panic equivalents  
• Feeling “on edge,” “one step from dropping everything” several nights/wk (Q6)

Pattern  
Persistent mood and anxiety symptoms most days × ≥2 wk; functional impact evident (feeding, household tasks, social withdrawal). Denies anhedonia absolutely (still laughs, though fleeting). Denies self-harm ideation (Q10).

Screening significance  
Meets provisional concern for:  
– Minor depressive episode with peripartum onset  
– Generalized/specific perinatal anxiety features (no avoidance, but physiologic arousal and intrusive worry)

Safety  
No suicidal or infanticidal ideation reported; no plan or intent.

Risk factors  
Primiparous, sleep deprivation, high self-expectations, no psychosocial supports mentioned.

Recommendation  
Continue monitoring; consider further assessment with EPDS, refer for counseling or psychiatric evaluation if symptoms persist ≥2 additional weeks or worsen.
